ybbfw: *"Mahalia, The Gospel Superstar"* is a vibrant mural honoring the legendary Mahalia Jackson, one of the most influential gospel singers of all time. The artwork captures her powerful presence, depicting her in a moment of deep emotion, eyes closed and hands raised as she sings. Rich, warm tones radiate from her figure, symbolizing the spirit and soul of gospel music. Surrounding her are visual elements representing her legacy—musical notes, church stained glass, and scenes from the civil rights movement, where her voice became a beacon of hope. This mural celebrates Mahalia Jackson’s enduring impact on music, faith, and social change.

w8v0k: Painted with the neighborhood residents, TILT (as it‘s popularly known) depicts a monumental racially mixed group of people protectively embracing their homes against a background of decorative patterns similar to old-fashioned wallpaper. While smaller figures “build” their community through work and play, others fend off drugs, vandalism, gangs, absentee landlords, real estate speculators, unemployment and freeways – all of which threaten the quality of life. These dark tilted images on the north half are meant to be seen only by the local audience; eastbound traffic on Fullerton sees only the positive harmonious images.
mkjr8: Internationally respected DOZE GREEN is the featured artist for the 2012 block-long Glenwood wall from Morse to Farwell. His mural, "The Digital Frontier" relates to the impact of technology on communication and the eternal creating and breaking of boundaries. Doze uses simple graphic imagery combined with complex layering and color movement to show the constant flux of realities, addressing the present moment and connecting it with the past and future. Light beams emanating from individual faces map the manifestation of ideas and the future, and arms are raised for the revolutions and uprisings. Waves show the movement of technology, language and science and windows within windows will represent limitations, barriers, privacy rights and global censorship.
